sources.title: Jesse Hemerik and Jelle Goeman, Exact Testing with Random Permutations
sources.locator: arXiv v3 full-text PDF, §§2.1–2.2 and 3.1–3.4; Definitions 1–2, complete proofs of Theorems 1–2 and Proposition 3, plus the out-of-scope Proposition 1 and Proposition 2 exactness results.

contents.name: Definition 1, permutation-invariance null and its finite transformation group
contents.reason: The local setup states the invariant-null premise explicitly and extends the action from finite sample spaces to measurable data spaces.

contents.name: Theorem 1 and both proofs, validity of the fixed full-group upper-tail test
contents.reason: The theorem locally proves superuniformity for the inclusive full-orbit rank without assuming a free action or a finite data space.

contents.name: Condition 1 and Proposition 1, exactness only on the tie-class significance grid
contents.reason: The assigned result randomizes uniformly within the boundary tie block and proves an exactly uniform p-value for every threshold, so the additional equal-size tie-class condition and grid restriction are not needed.

contents.name: Equation (3), exact boundary randomization for a full-group test with tied scores
contents.reason: The local theorem computes the conditional rejection probability by clipping the uniform tie-block threshold and proves exact null rejection probability.

contents.name: Section 2.2, the inclusive full-group rank as a weakly valid p-value and the non-uniqueness caveat
contents.reason: The local theorem proves the weak superuniform inequality under each invariant null law rather than claiming one unique null distribution for the score.

contents.name: Section 3.1, distinction between Monte Carlo tests and random transformations with the observed identity
contents.reason: The local proof uses group recentering and finite ranks; it does not assume the transformed observations are independent conditional on the null.

contents.name: Section 3.2, the uncorrected random-permutation estimate can have a positive atom at zero and exceed its cutoff error
contents.reason: The companion counterexample gives an invariant two-point model with exact probability 1/4 at zero and violates superuniformity at cutoff zero.

contents.name: Definition 2, identity adjoined to random transformations sampled with or without replacement
contents.reason: The algorithm states both simulation designs separately, including the uniform-subset constraint B≤|G|−1 without replacement.

contents.name: Theorem 2 and direct rank proof, identity-corrected random-permutation test validity
contents.reason: The local theorem proves the plus-one upper-tail formula by recentering the identity-containing list, retaining ties and transformation multiplicities.

contents.name: Proposition 2, exact grid results under equal-sized score-equivalence classes
contents.reason: The assigned Monte Carlo claims require only superuniformity with ties; the extra score-class condition for exact grid levels is stronger and not used.

contents.name: Proposition 3 and proof, randomizing a Monte Carlo threshold tie to obtain exact rejection probability
contents.reason: The assigned Monte Carlo result proves superuniformity of the identity-corrected p-value and does not add this separate exact randomized threshold-tie procedure.

contents.name: Section 3.3 finite-subset construction for sampling from a possibly infinite group
contents.reason: The controlling design and local algorithms require a finite transformation group and make no uniform-sampling claim for an infinite group.

contents.name: Section 3.4, identity correction and superuniform upper-tail p-value for random transformations
contents.reason: The local definitions and theorem give the with-replacement and uniform-subset designs and prove their finite-sample superuniform bounds.

contents.name: Section 3.4, the additional tie-randomized Monte Carlo p-value that is exactly uniform
contents.reason: The assigned random-permutation theorem covers the identity-corrected inclusive p-value; this further randomized Monte Carlo p-value is not part of the planned claims.

contents.name: Section 2.1 invariant-null premise and the warning that non-group transformations can invalidate a test
contents.reason: The published counterexample on the earlier finite-group page records a concrete failure when invariance or the group premise is absent.

sources.title: Eugene Katsevich, STAT 9610 Lecture Notes
sources.locator: Full 132-page course notes; §3.2.4.2, printed pp. 54–56 / PDF pp. 57–59, equations (3.12)–(3.20), the IID-pairs exchangeability argument, and the stated identity-corrected Monte Carlo bound and warning.

contents.name: Permutation invariance under the IID-pairs independence null and the full-permutation upper-tail p-value, equations (3.12)–(3.17)
contents.reason: The example supplies an explicit two-sample Bernoulli null, verifies swap invariance, and computes the full-orbit ranks including tied outcomes.

contents.name: Identity plus independently sampled transformations and the (B+1) denominator, equations (3.18)–(3.20)
contents.reason: The notes state the identity-corrected formula and finite-sample bound and warn against omitting the correction; their proof says only 'Similar logic as above', so the complete group-recentering proof is supplied locally rather than attributed to this source.

contents.name: Warning that omitting the identity correction can give zero and exceed a prescribed type-I cutoff
contents.reason: The finite witness calculates the zero probability exactly and exhibits the superuniformity failure.

contents.name: Two-sample pooled-label permutation application and the source's independence-null scope
contents.reason: The worked example is explicitly under a common Bernoulli law and does not generalize the result to a weak mean null or an assignment law.

contents.name: Regression-specific strengths and limitations outside the exchangeability proof
contents.reason: The assigned pair proves finite-group invariance validity and the exact Monte Carlo rank; regression-model comparisons and other application-specific limitations are not claims of this page.
